entries.sense_en: acting as if you are better than other people

synonyms.nuance: Most common everyday word; stresses overconfidence in one's own ability or importance.
Can be positive (proud of your work); negative only when it means too much self-respect.
synonyms.example: too proud to ask for help

synonyms.nuance: Informal; looking down on others for social class or taste.

entries.tip_ko: gh는 소리 나지 않아 ‘호티’에 가깝게 발음한다.

entries.sense_en: also; in addition

synonyms.nuance: Neutral everyday word; likewise sounds more formal or bookish.
Stresses that two things are alike, not just that one is added.

entries.sense_en: greater than any other; with no equal

synonyms.nuance: Very close; often used for skill or quality in competition.
Never happened before; about events in time, not personal qualities.
So good it cannot be compared; slightly more emotional and poetic.

entries.sense_en: a person's usual character or mood (here, not anger)

synonyms.nuance: Modern neutral word for someone's natural character; temper today usually means anger.
Formal; a person's typical attitude toward life and people.
Simplest, broadest word for what someone is basically like.
synonyms.example: It's not in her nature to lie.

entries.modern: sweetness of temper → a sweet nature
entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 temper는 주로 ‘화, 성질’(lose one’s temper)을 뜻하니 옛 의미와 구별하자.

entries.sense_en: here, an old word for stepmother: her father's new wife

synonyms.nuance: The correct modern word for a father's new wife.
synonyms.example: She lives with her father and stepmother.

synonyms.nuance: Today only your husband's or wife's mother.

entries.modern: mother-in-law → stepmother
entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서 mother-in-law는 ‘시어머니·장모’만 뜻한다.

entries.match: show herself in her true colors
entries.sense_en: to reveal your real, usually bad, character

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; does not suggest the hidden side is bad.
synonyms.example: He finally revealed himself as the leader.

synonyms.nuance: Suggests a brief, accidental moment of honesty rather than a full reveal.
synonyms.example: For a moment, she let the mask slip.

entries.modern: show her true colors

entries.sense_en: very unpleasant and hateful

synonyms.nuance: Plainer word; can also describe a person full of hate.
Formal; causes a strong feeling of disgust, often moral.
Everyday; annoying and offensive in behavior rather than deeply evil.

entries.sense_en: low in status; poor and humble (not unkind)

synonyms.nuance: Low in rank or importance, often with a sense of humility.
Used for boring, unskilled work, especially servants' jobs.
For clothes or places: worn out and in poor condition.

entries.modern: the meanest work → the lowliest chores
entries.tip_ko: mean은 ‘못된’뿐 아니라 옛 글에서 ‘천한, 초라한’ 뜻으로 자주 쓰인다(mean apparel, meanly dressed).

entries.sense_en: cleaned by rubbing very hard

synonyms.nuance: Very close; scrub is more common and often uses a brush and water.
Rubbing to make something shine, not to remove dirt.
Light, quick cleaning with a cloth; no hard rubbing.

entries.sense_en: a small, poor room at the top of a house, under the roof

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for the roof space, usually used for storage.
An open upper space; today often a stylish apartment.

entries.modern: garret → attic room

entries.sense_en: very poor in quality; miserable

synonyms.nuance: Common; describes feelings or conditions that make people unhappy.
Makes you feel pity; can also mean embarrassingly poor.
Dirty and unpleasant because of poverty or neglect.

entries.tip_ko: -ed는 /ɪd/로 두 음절, ‘레치드’.

entries.sense_en: an old use: scolded her sharply

synonyms.nuance: Common word for angrily telling someone off, often a child.
synonyms.example: Mom scolded me for being late.

synonyms.nuance: Informal, everyday British and American phrase.

entries.modern: would have rattled her off → would have scolded her
entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 rattle off는 ‘줄줄 읊다’(rattle off a list)라는 뜻이다.

entries.sense_en: in spite of

synonyms.nuance: Standard neutral word; notwithstanding is formal or legal.
Same meaning, slightly more emphatic and conversational.

entries.sense_en: clothes

synonyms.nuance: Neutral general word; apparel is formal or used in stores.
Formal; often about clothes suited to an occasion.
Individual pieces of clothing; used in trade and literature.

entries.sense_en: to make a strong impression by how you look

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase; simply be noticeable, good or bad.
Informal; create sudden excitement or attention.
synonyms.example: The new singer made a splash.

entries.modern: cut a dashing figure (still used, a bit literary)

entries.sense_en: very; greatly

synonyms.nuance: Neutral modern intensifier.
Informal and modern; often with verbs like enjoy or succeed.

entries.modern: mightily delighted → really delighted

entries.sense_en: to look good on someone; to suit them

synonyms.nuance: Common modern word for clothes or colors that look good on you.
Makes someone look more attractive than usual.

entries.modern: as might become them → that would suit them
entries.tip_ko: become이 ‘되다’가 아니라 ‘어울리다’로 쓰인 예. becoming은 ‘잘 어울리는’.

entries.sense_en: to make up for something bad or lacking

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb; same idea, less formal.
synonyms.example: to make up for lost time

synonyms.nuance: Formal; often about money or balancing a weakness.
Serious, moral or religious; for a real wrong or sin.

entries.tip_ko: amends는 항상 -s가 붙은 형태로 쓴다.

entries.sense_en: a word showing sadness or regret

synonyms.nuance: Modern everyday way to express regret about a fact.
Neutral, common in writing and speech; less emotional.

entries.modern: Alas! → Oh, no… / Sadly,

entries.sense_en: to laugh at someone rudely; to mock

synonyms.nuance: General word for making fun of someone unkindly.
Can be playful and friendly, not always hurtful.
synonyms.example: She teased him about his hair.

synonyms.nuance: Deliberately trying to hurt or provoke someone.

entries.modern: you only jeer me → you're just making fun of me
entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 보통 jeer at someone처럼 at을 붙인다.

entries.sense_en: to that place; there

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word.
Also old-fashioned; means over there, at a distance you can see.

entries.modern: thither → there
entries.tip_ko: hither(이리로)–thither(저리로) 짝으로 기억하자.

entries.sense_en: correct; right about something

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word: You're right.
Having a good reason for an action or feeling.

entries.modern: Thou art in the right of it → You're right about that

entries.sense_en: crookedly; badly, not in the right position

synonyms.nuance: Everyday adjective for something not straight.
Slightly to one side; a bit formal or written.
Plain word; awry is common in 'go awry' (plans fail).

entries.tip_ko: ‘어-라이’로 발음한다(‘오리’ 아님). go awry = 일이 틀어지다.

entries.sense_en: carried away by a very strong feeling of happiness

synonyms.nuance: Modern, very common word for extreme happiness.
synonyms.example: We were overjoyed at the news.

synonyms.nuance: Extremely excited and happy, often loudly so.
High-spirited, often after a success.

entries.sense_en: began to cry

synonyms.nuance: Sudden and strong; today's natural phrase.
Lose emotional control, usually after holding feelings in.
synonyms.example: He broke down at the funeral.

entries.modern: fell a-crying → started crying
entries.tip_ko: a-crying, a-laughing의 a-는 옛 표현으로 ‘~하는 중’을 뜻한다.

entries.sense_en: to find a clever way to make something happen

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; plan and organize something.
Succeed in doing something difficult.
Invent a plan or method, usually carefully.

entries.tip_ko: contrived(형용사)는 ‘억지스러운, 부자연스러운’이라는 부정적 뜻이다.

entries.sense_en: took out the inside with a spoon or hand

synonyms.nuance: Stresses the empty shape that results.
Removing something by digging, often with effort.

entries.sense_en: the thick, hard outer skin of a fruit or vegetable

synonyms.nuance: Skin you remove, especially of oranges or bananas.
Thin outer layer, as on an apple or grape.
Hard covering of nuts, eggs or sea animals.

entries.sense_en: covered with a thin layer of gold

synonyms.nuance: Technical: a thin gold coat over cheaper metal.
Adjective form; common for frames and book edges.

entries.tip_ko: guild(조합)와 발음이 같다.

entries.sense_en: not knowing what to do or where to find something

synonyms.nuance: Informal; unable to go on with a task.
Confused because you don't understand something.
Special use: too surprised to speak.
synonyms.example: I was at a loss for words.

entries.sense_en: saw; looked at

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern verb.
See an event happen, often an important one.
Literary; look long and admiringly.

entries.modern: eyes ever beheld → anyone had ever seen

entries.sense_en: special uniforms worn by servants of a rich family

synonyms.nuance: General word for clothes a group must wear.
Clothes for a play, party or a particular period.

entries.tip_ko: liver(간)와 관련 없는 단어다.

entries.sense_en: thickly covered or decorated (all over)

synonyms.nuance: Spread messily, usually with something dirty or greasy.
Neutral; no sense of excess.
Informal; covered thickly, often too much.

entries.sense_en: a fine carriage with horses and servants

synonyms.nuance: Just the vehicle pulled by horses.
A large closed carriage; today also a bus.
Related modern word: tools or gear for a purpose.

entries.sense_en: covered or decorated all over (with jewels)

synonyms.nuance: Modern word for jewels or metal points set into a surface.
Covered with a hard layer, often of jewels.

entries.modern: beset with jewels → studded with jewels
entries.tip_ko: 현대에는 주로 ‘(문제가) 따라다니다’(beset by problems) 뜻으로 쓴다.

entries.sense_en: dressed or decorated in a fine, special way

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase for wearing nicer clothes than usual.
synonyms.example: all dressed up for the party

synonyms.nuance: Formal; decorated with beautiful things.

entries.sense_en: got down from a vehicle

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase for cars and carriages.
Used for buses, trains, bikes and horses.
Get down from a horse or bicycle.

entries.tip_ko: 형용사 alight는 ‘불타는’(set alight)이라는 전혀 다른 뜻이다.

entries.sense_en: very deep and complete

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; profound sounds more serious and formal.
Stresses completeness, not depth.
Very strong, often about feelings.

entries.sense_en: to look at something carefully for a long time

synonyms.nuance: Look for a long time, often with love or wonder.
Look closely to learn or understand details.
Think carefully, not look; contemplate can mean both.

entries.tip_ko: 강세는 첫음절 CON-.

entries.sense_en: unusual and remarkable

synonyms.nuance: Common; worth noticing because unusual.
Stronger; far beyond the normal.
Strange in an odd, often negative way.

entries.tip_ko: 문법 용어 ‘단수’ 외에 ‘비범한’ 뜻도 있다.

entries.sense_en: a light meal of cold food

synonyms.nuance: Modern word for snacks and drinks at an event.
Food set out for guests to serve themselves.

entries.modern: collation → refreshments

entries.sense_en: a very small piece of food

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word: the amount you bite at once.
Tiny dry bit, especially of bread or cake.
Small leftover piece, often of waste food.

entries.sense_en: looking steadily for a long time, with love or wonder

synonyms.nuance: Long fixed look, often rude or shocked.
A very quick look.
Stare with the mouth open in surprise.

entries.sense_en: polite acts or kind words

synonyms.nuance: Warmer; shows respect and kindness.
General uncountable word for good manners.
Small polite remarks in conversation.

entries.sense_en: an old spelling of curtsy: a small bow a woman makes by bending her knees

synonyms.nuance: The modern spelling for this bow.
Bending from the waist; usually done by men.

entries.modern: made a courtesy → curtsied
entries.tip_ko: 여기서는 ‘예의’가 아니라 curtsy(무릎 굽혀 인사)이다.

entries.sense_en: hurried

synonyms.nuance: Normal modern verb.
Formal verb from the same root, still used today.
Stronger; very fast, sometimes careless.

entries.modern: hasted away → hurried away

entries.sense_en: opening the mouth wide, here as in a yawn

synonyms.nuance: Exactly the tired mouth-opening; gape is broader.
Informal; stare stupidly, not about yawning.

entries.sense_en: a feeling of wanting to do something

synonyms.nuance: Stronger wish.
Sudden strong feeling, often hard to control.
What usually happens, not a wish.

entries.sense_en: showing no interest or concern

synonyms.nuance: Simply not interested; less cold.
Not worried about something.
Negative; lacking energy or care in general.

entries.tip_ko: ‘다르지 않은’이 아니라 ‘무관심한’. 강세는 -DIF-.

entries.sense_en: to be in a difficult situation

synonyms.nuance: Informal; in trouble with no easy way out.
Finding something difficult to do.

entries.modern: sadly put to it → in real trouble

entries.sense_en: as a joke; not seriously

synonyms.nuance: Modern everyday equivalent.
In a light, fun and teasing way.

entries.modern: jestingly → jokingly

entries.sense_en: quick and light in movement

synonyms.nuance: Moves easily and quickly; also used for businesses.
Plain word about speed only, not lightness.
Active and lively, usually about old people.

entries.sense_en: beautiful, expensive clothes and jewelry

synonyms.nuance: Plain phrase; the best things you own to wear.
Informal and humorous.

entries.tip_ko: ‘파이너리’로 발음(fine에서 온 말).

entries.sense_en: an old word for a young woman of a low class or a servant girl

synonyms.nuance: Neutral modern word.
Old: young woman; modern: female servant.
Friendly regional word, especially Scottish and northern English.

entries.modern: country wench → country girl
entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 wench는 낮잡는 말로 들리니 쓰지 않는다. Cinderwench도 같은 말에서 왔다.

entries.sense_en: amused; entertained

synonyms.nuance: Neutral modern word.
Make someone smile or laugh.

entries.modern: well diverted → had a good time
entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 divert는 주로 ‘방향을 돌리다’(divert traffic) 뜻이다.

entries.sense_en: announced publicly and officially

synonyms.nuance: Common neutral word for telling people news.
Formal, strong statement; often official.

entries.sense_en: to push hard and suddenly

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; no idea of force or speed.
Push roughly, often rudely.
Force into a tight space.

entries.tip_ko: 과거·과거분사도 thrust. th는 /θ/.

entries.sense_en: to tease; to make fun of someone

synonyms.nuance: Make fun of someone, playfully or unkindly.
Clearly unkind making fun.

entries.modern: banter her → tease her (today banter is friendly joking between people)
entries.tip_ko: 현대의 banter는 주로 명사로 ‘친근한 농담 주고받기’를 뜻한다.

entries.sense_en: rooms to live in

synonyms.nuance: Formal general word for a place to stay.
Rooms given to servants, soldiers or staff.
